first_hunter_context.bar: Company guide for Q2 FY27: subscription revenue $264-268M, non-GAAP EBIT margin ~20% (Q1 FY27 release, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001169561/000116956126000020/q1fy27pressrelease.htm). Sell-side consensus: total revenue $310.8M, EPS $1.25, unrevised over 30 days (Zacks via Yahoo, 2026-10-22, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/unlocking-q2-potential-commvault-cvlt-121507687.html). A second aggregator agrees at $310.28M / $1.24 (https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/10/25/commvault-systems-cvlt-expected-to-post-earnings-on-tuesday.html). Zacks's subscription line ($263.16M) uses a different definition from the restated company line, so I size against the company guide. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against the $266M subscription midpoint.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest is about 7.7% of float with 4.3 days to cover (Equibles, as of 2026-08-19, https://equibles.com/stocks/cvlt/summary). Another source shows 3.21M shares and 5.59 days at the 2026-08-14 settlement (https://altindex.com/ticker/cvlt/short-interest). I found no October settlement. That is moderate, not crowded. Skew_25d is -6.05 vol points, meaning calls are bid ('upside paid'), but the chain is thin: 270 total open interest and an ATM spread of 19% of mid. Part of the call bid is probably takeover optionality, since a sale process has been reported as open since April, rather than a view on the print. Run-up is +13.0% over 20 days and +9.5% over 5. Analyst targets were raised into the print: Scotiabank $160 (10-05), RBC $160 (10-08), Mizuho $185 (10-12/15), Baird $180 (10-19), Cantor $171 (10-26), Jefferies $170 Hold (10-26). Spot of $167.36 is above the MarketBeat/StockAnalysis average target of $160.7-163.5.

evidence.text: Q2 subscription revenue is guided to $264-268M, flat to down from Q1's actual $267.0M, and Q1 term-license revenue grew only +1% while management cited a term-duration headwind as customers assessed hardware/storage plans. On its own record Commvault guides conservatively: Q1 beat EPS $1.42 vs $1.16 and revenue $314.1M vs $310.5M. A beat of the $266M midpoint by ~1-2% is therefore the base case, but that is a quarter the company told the market to expect.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats have been sold. Q1 FY27 (2026-07-28): EPS beat by $0.26 and revenue beat, stock -19.7% on the flat sequential subscription guide. 2026-01-27: -31.1%. 2025-10-28: -16.3%. Only 2026-04-28 (+10.8%) paid for a beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Consensus already sits at the guide ($310.8M total revenue), and a beat of a conservative guide is the expected outcome. Had the market priced a large upside surprise, Zacks's EPS estimate would have been revised up in the last 30 days; it was not.
evidence.independence: The term-duration/hardware comment comes from a secondary summary of the 2026-07-28 call, which shares the event with this release (https://www.tickerreport.com/?p=13519146, 404 at fetch; quoted in search snippet). The July sell-off rationale is in https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/07/28/why-commvault-stock-crashed-today/

evidence.text: Rubrik, the closest listed cyber-resilience/backup peer, reported its July quarter on 2026-08-27, after Commvault last spoke. It exceeded every guided metric, raised every FY27 metric, and grew subscription ARR to $1.66B with net new subscription ARR +35% YoY and Cloud ARR +39%. That points to healthy category demand through Commvault's September quarter, especially for SaaS ARR (Commvault Q1 SaaS ARR $424M, +38%).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No direct history of CVLT reacting to Rubrik prints is in the baseline. CVLT's ARR/guide line drove the -19.7% in July and the +10.8% in April.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The 20-day run-up and the October target raises probably already carry some sector read-through. Had it been fully priced, Commvault's FY27 subscription ARR consensus would sit above the $1,200-1,210M guide, and I found no source showing that. Rubrik also takes share partly from Commvault, so the read is a category proxy, not a company number.
evidence.independence: Proxy. Rubrik's own release corroborates it: https://www.rubrik.com/company/newsroom/press-releases/26/rubrik-reports-second-quarter-fiscal-year-2027-financial-results (403 at fetch, figures via https://pulse2.com/rubrik-cloud-arr-jumps-39-to-1-48-billion-as-subscription-arr-contribution-margin-expands-460-basis-points/)

evidence.text: NetApp's July quarter (reported late Aug/early Sep 2026) showed revenue +30%, all-flash +47%, a raised FY27 guide and customers accelerating purchases as component costs rose. That is relevant to the on-prem/term-license line Commvault said was soft because customers were 'assessing hardware and storage plans'. A completed storage refresh would tend to unlock the attached backup term license in the September quarter.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 term-license revenue +1% YoY was part of the guide disappointment that preceded the -19.7% move. There is no earlier history of CVLT reacting to the storage cycle in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The macro-to-company transmission has not been confirmed by Commvault, and pulled-forward hardware buying can also delay software decisions. If priced, the sell-side would have lifted Commvault's term-license estimates; Zacks shows no EPS revision in 30 days.
evidence.independence: Proxy, and it shares the storage-cycle theme with nothing else here. Dell's record storage revenue (+26%) points the same way: https://www.cnhinews.com/news/article_5d680f27-4b3d-50ba-bdc5-90a4de5f6a40.html

evidence.text: Into the print the stock is +9.5% over 5 sessions and +13.0% over 20, within 4% of its 52-week high and above the average analyst target ($160.7-163.5). Six target raises landed between 5 and 26 Oct, three of them from Neutral/Hold houses chasing the price (Cantor $132→$171, Jefferies $130→$170, Scotiabank $130→$160). This repeats the July set-up: Truist raised to $182 a week before, then a beat with a flat guide sold off -19.7%. A print that only meets the bar has room to fall.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a 92% rally into July, a beat with a soft guide gave -19.7%. Of the last four prints, three fell by 16-31%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The option market leans the other way: skew -6.05, with calls bid. So the market is paying for upside, not hedging a give-back. The reason I think the option market is wrong about this print is that the chain is thin (270 OI, ATM spread 19% of mid) and its call bid more plausibly prices takeover optionality than the quarter. Short interest of ~7.7% / 4-6 days is not crowded enough to make a squeeze the dominant mechanism.
evidence.independence: Jefferies Hold at $170, 2026-10-26: https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9142359/cvlt-maintained-by-jefferies-price-target-raised-to-170 . Baird/RBC/Mizuho raises: https://www.cnn.com/markets/stocks/CVLT . Run-up from the sealed baseline.

evidence.text: Reuters reported on 2026-04-10 that Commvault is exploring a sale with Goldman Sachs after takeover interest, including an earlier offer from Thoma Bravo. No company statement or 8-K has closed the process since: EDGAR shows only an 8-K adding director David Morton, the CFO of Intapp, on 2026-09-22, with no mention of it, and an August report says no decision has been made. Companies often disclose a deal or an end to the review alongside results, so the print carries a two-sided tail.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose ~13-17% on the day of the Reuters report (2026-04-10, to $88.52). There is no history of a print carrying deal news.
evidence.why_not_priced: The probability that anything is said on 27 Oct is unknowable from public documents. Some deal premium is already in a stock that has roughly doubled since April. If the market expected an announcement with the print, the event-implied move (12.2%) would sit well above the name's 16.3% median reaction rather than below it.
evidence.independence: The August status update (no final decision; may remain independent): https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/software/nasdaq-cvlt/commvault-systems/news/commvault-sale-talks-put-mixed-shareholder-returns-in-fresh . The director 8-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1169561/000116956126000030/cvlt-20260922.htm

evidence.text: Insiders sold 29,348 shares (~$4.2M) in the three months after the July print, under 10b5-1 plans and largely for tax withholding (CEO 12,437 shares at $143.98 on 08-17). EDGAR shows a cluster of Form 144s on 08-10 and 08-17/20 and no open-market buys.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None in the baseline.
evidence.why_not_priced: Routine and public. It is filed because it is a sourced fact, and sized near zero because these are scheduled tax-withholding sales.
evidence.independence: The MarketBeat summary of the same Form 4s, so the same documents: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/analyst-commvault-systems-nasdaq-cvlt-stock-price-expected-to-rise-cantor-fitzgerald-analyst-says-2026-10-26/

evidence.text: Commvault security advisories AV26-895/899 (Canadian Cyber Centre, Commvault Cloud vulnerabilities patched in 11.36.123/11.40.72/11.44.20/11.46.20)
Zacks subscription-revenue consensus of $263.16M, below the low end of the $264M guide, which would make a beat look larger
Cause of the 2026-10-21 +4.9% day and the sector rally. GuruFocus names no catalyst, and the Alphastreet article returned 403.
Any October 2026 report on the sale process (Reuters/Bloomberg). None found after April; the latest is the Simply Wall St note of 2026-08-14.
The full Q1 FY27 call transcript, for the exact Q2 total-revenue guide and the term-duration wording. Only secondary summaries were found (stocktaper 429, tickerreport 404).
October short-interest settlement. Only July/August figures were found.
Commvault price increases or customer renewal complaints in 2026. Nothing found; Q3 FY26 restructuring is old news.
The Board Operating Committee chaired by Morton is an existing committee with a July 2024 charter, not a new activist structure.

first_hunter_context.bar: Disputed, so every size is capped small. Q3 2026 revenue consensus is $139.5m with EPS -$0.21 (Zacks, 1 estimate, via CNHI after the Q2 print: https://www.cnhinews.com/news/article_f9d8e36c-e7dd-54cf-9eb2-72380e6de503.html), $77.4m with non-GAAP EPS -$0.43 (Benzinga: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/DQ/earnings-forecasts) and EPS -$0.48 (TipRanks). The Q2 bar was also disputed after the fact: finviz cited $114.7m revenue and -$0.53 EPS, Earnings Whispers $59.2m and -$0.28. There is no company revenue guide, only production guidance: Q3 40,000-45,000 MT and FY2026 160,000-180,000 MT (Q2 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001477641/000110465926099218/tm2623691d1_ex99-1.htm). print_vs_bar is my inference: roughly 25-30k MT sold at about $4.7-5.0/kg, i.e. $120-145m, against a bar midpoint of about $108m.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest was 4,399,192 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, about 6.5% of the 67.67m ADS outstanding, with 6.56 days to cover. The peak was 5.05m on 2026-09-15, and short interest has roughly doubled from 2.1m in Oct 2025 (https://equibles.com/stocks/dq/shortinterest, read 2026-10-26). That is moderately crowded on days to cover, not extreme. In the sealed baseline, skew_25d is -6.19 vol points (upside paid) and the put/call OI ratio is 4.79. The event-implied move is 12.2%, but the ATM spread is 75% of mid, so that figure is indicative only. Spot is $10.11: -7.25% over 20 days, 0.3% above the 52-week low, 71.7% below the 52-week high. Goldman's Sell rating carries a $10 target (stockanalysis.com).

evidence.text: China n-type rod polysilicon transaction prices (Silicon Industry Branch) rose from RMB 32,000/t in the week of 22 Jul to RMB 43,000/t in the week of 17-23 Sep (+34%), and held at 43,000 through the 21 Oct weekly print. So Q3 realised ASP should sit clearly above Q2's $4.04/kg (cash cost $4.57, total cost $5.95). Inventory marked to NRV at Q2-end prices (Q2 impairment $55.7m) is now being sold above its carrying value, which points to a smaller impairment and a narrower gross loss than Q2's $82.7m. Q4 opens at the higher price.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: DQ has not paid for revenue or margin lines lately. Q4'25 (26 Feb 2026) beat on EPS and still fell 6.85% intraday on a revenue miss (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/1145858192). Q1'26 (29 Apr) fell 11.85% (sealed tape; the volume spike confirms the event day). Q2'26 (20 Aug) fell 14.6% on an EPS miss despite a sequential revenue rise (https://finviz.com/news/383985/daqo-new-energy-shares-tumble-after-q2-earnings-miss-and-weak-polysilicon-market).
evidence.why_not_priced: The industry price is public. Yet DQ fell 7.25% over 20 days to within 0.3% of its 52-week low while the price it sells at rose about a third, so the tape is not carrying the ASP improvement. The consensus EPS range of -$0.21 to -$0.48 is far narrower than Q2's -$1.20 and may partly carry it. If it were fully priced, the stock would have recovered off the post-Q2 lows rather than making new ones.
evidence.independence: The 21 Oct weekly report confirms prices flat at 43,000 (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768). On the Q2 call (20 Aug) management cited transactions near RMB 40/kg and said spot was beginning to recover (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262122110-tradingkey). Both are proxies; there is no company Q3 ASP.

evidence.text: Q3 sales volume is the swing line, and the evidence points both ways; net slightly positive. On 20 Aug management said shipments 'continued to pick up in the third quarter', that 'selling and shipping our product is really not an issue', and that it targets about 15% market share and lower inventory. Q2 sales were only 15,190 MT against 43,675 MT produced, and H1 was 87.1k produced against 19.7k sold. Against that, the industry's weekly reports show thin spot trade: the 28 Sep release was the first official price in almost two months, only 2-4 firms were transacting, and new orders were slow as of 21 Oct. A revenue bar of $77-140m implies roughly 16-29k MT at about $4.8/kg, so modest volume growth clears the low end. If Q3 sales stay well below the 40-45k MT production, the inventory and cash-burn worry continues.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Volume drove the last two prints. In Q1'26, sales of 4,482 MT against 38,167 MT in Q4'25 coincided with -11.85%. In Q2'26 volume recovered to 15,190 MT but ASP fell, and the stock dropped 14.6%.
evidence.why_not_priced: No Q3 volume figure has been published. Xinjiang Daqo (688303) releases its Q3 report on 2026-10-28 per its disclosure calendar (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/688303/event.html), so the number arrives with DQ's own release. Consensus revenue spans almost 2x ($77m-$140m), which is what an unresolved volume line looks like.
evidence.independence: The counter-evidence on thin spot trade comes from different sources: https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260928/c680289466.shtml and https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768. H1 production and sales come from Pacific Securities' interim note (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H3_AP202609221829741877_1.pdf, 2026-09-22, snippet only).

evidence.text: Industry production cuts began in October: the Silicon Industry Branch expects utilization of about 35% from October, and a 30 Sep weekly projected October output of about 105k t, down 12.9% month on month. DQ's Q4 production guide is therefore likely to come in at the low end of, or below, what the FY guide implies (FY 160-180k MT less H1 87.1k and Q3 40-45k leaves about 28-53k MT for Q4). That supports price, but at about 57% of nameplate capacity already, a lower utilisation raises unit cost and idle-capacity charges, and the market has sold DQ's lower-volume quarters.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Feb 2026 the FY26 production guide (140-170k MT) came with a revenue miss and the stock fell about 6.9%. No print in the history isolates a production-guide cut.
evidence.why_not_priced: Industry-level cuts are public; DQ's own Q4 number is not. Its 9 Oct IR record said only that it will set its pace by market supply and demand (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1643057.shtml). The sign of the market's reading of a cut, price support or unit-cost drag, is not observable in advance.
evidence.independence: The 9 Oct Xinjiang Daqo IR record calls 'actual output changes' the core industry variable (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1643057.shtml). The October output projection comes from https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026093000036747 (2026-09-30, snippet only).

evidence.text: Positioning leans toward a squeeze on any non-negative print. Short interest is 4.4m shares (about 6.5% of ADS), days to cover 6.56 at the 30 Sep settlement, roughly double a year ago. The stock is 0.3% above its 52-week low and at Goldman's $10 Sell target, and the option skew pays for upside (-6.19 vol points).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints all fell (-6.9%, -11.9%, -14.6%) with short interest lower than now. No squeeze has shown up on a print in this history.
evidence.why_not_priced: Skew and price already show it: upside is paid and the stock is at its lows. This is a modest positive on how a near-bar print could trade, not an unpriced fact.
evidence.independence: Skew comes from the sealed baseline (Yahoo options); the Goldman $10 Sell target from https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/dq/. Different data from the same theme.

evidence.text: Market cap is about $686m (67.67m ADS x $10.11) against $1.92bn of cash, short-term investments, bank notes, HTM and fixed deposits and zero debt at 30 Jun (Q2 6-K), part of it attributable to Xinjiang Daqo's minority holders. The Q2 release disclosed no active ADS repurchase program, only $7.8m of buybacks at the subsidiary. A new ADS buyback or a capital-return statement on the call would land on a stock trading well below its cash.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No capital-return announcement in the reaction history I could establish.
evidence.why_not_priced: The discount to cash is long-known and priced as cash trapped in China and pledged to AIDC diversification. Only an announcement inside the window would change it, and I found no source saying one is coming, so this is sized as an option, not an expectation.
evidence.independence: The 9 Oct IR coverage cites about RMB 10.4bn of cash and a 7.9% debt ratio at Xinjiang Daqo (https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1643057.shtml).

evidence.text: Cash is being steered into diversification. In June Xinjiang Daqo committed about RMB 6bn to a Kunshan AIDC energy-systems manufacturing base. Per the 9 Oct IR coverage the project is still at the early permitting stage and the R&D is early, so any capex or progress update on the call is a use of the cash a value holder wants returned.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The A-share hit limit-up on the 4 Jun 2026 announcement (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/688303/event.html). There is no print-day reaction to this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the announcement is four months old. Only a capex number or a funding change on the call would be new.
evidence.independence: Q2 call coverage (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/DQ) notes the AIDC power-equipment entry via affiliate Daqo Group.

evidence.text: Downstream demand is weak: China's Jan-Jul 2026 new PV installations were 86.15 GW, -61% year on year, and chain-wide inventory was estimated at about 500k t in early September. That caps how far the price recovery passes through to Q4 volumes and to the outlook management gives.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 20 Aug management deferred the market's improvement to 2027, and the stock fell 14.6% that day.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is a public macro series, and the stock at its lows reflects it. It is filed as a proxy for the outlook commentary.
evidence.independence: Proxy, snippet only. The 21 Oct weekly cites a downstream price inversion blocking pass-through (https://wap.stockstar.com/detail/IG2026102100037768).

evidence.text: The baseline's 8-event reaction history (median |move| 2.84%) as an earnings base rate.
Earnings-site claim that DQ fell only 1.83% after Q1 2026.
Separate finding: management said Q3 shipments were picking up.
BusinessAnalytiq Northeast Asia polysilicon index at $4.95/kg for Sept 2026, +9.8%.
A Q3 volume or ASP figure from Daqo or Xinjiang Daqo before the print: none. The 688303 Q3 report is scheduled for 2026-10-28, and the 9 Oct IR record gives no numbers.
A Q3 2026 print from a peer polysilicon producer (Tongwei, Wacker, GCL) before 27 Oct: none found.
A dated sell-side Q3 preview for DQ from late October: none found.
An active DQ ADS buyback authorisation in 2026: none in the Q2 release or the search results.
The polysilicon consolidation (收储) platform's October execution: nothing concrete found.
Short interest for the 15 Oct settlement: not yet published (FINRA due 26 Oct).

Average 20-day volume is 28.5m shares, so 96m+ short is about 3-4 days. This is a crowded short at an all-time low, with the options market paying for a crash tail.

evidence.text: Q3 is largely pre-released, but the fuel assumption is likely a little light. JetBlue's 2026-09-10 update guided Q3 fuel at $3.96/gal off the 2026-09-04 Brent curve, with CASM ex-fuel raised to +6-8% for ATC and weather. Southwest's Q3 fuel came in at $3.92 against its own prior $3.70-3.75 assumption, so late-quarter fuel ran above earlier curves. JetBlue is unhedged, so an overshoot of $0.05-0.10/gal on ~220m gallons is about $11-22m, or $0.03-0.06 a share, against a -$0.53 bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Baseline reactions: +10.5% (Q2 2026), +1.21%, -6.89%, -11.86%, +6.65%, +2.7%, -25.71%. The reported quarter was pre-released in September, so this line has mostly been seen already.
evidence.why_not_priced: The $3.96 figure is the company's own and is what the bar is built on. The Southwest overshoot (published 2026-10-21) suggests the late-September curve ran higher. If that were priced, consensus would sit below the guide-implied loss; the single available consensus, -$0.53, is roughly at it. Small, and inside a quarter the company has already described.

evidence.text: The Q4 guide will be built on fuel far above anything JetBlue has guided this year. United guided Q4 at $4.80/gal (2026-10-21, Q4 EPS $0.50-1.50 vs ~$1.76-1.88 consensus), Southwest at ~$4.55/gal off the 2026-10-15 curve (Q4 EPS $0.55-0.80 vs $0.82 est.), and UBS models JetBlue at $4.85. JetBlue's Q3 guide was $3.96 and its July full-year guide assumed $3.49 with -2% to -5% operating margin, so the FY guide must be cut or suspended and Q4 will show a deep operating loss. JetBlue has no hedges.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 brought a weak outlook plus better-than-expected fuel recapture (nearly 50% recaptured), and the stock went +10.5%. The Q3 2025 print brought -11.86% and Q4 2024 brought -25.71%; the baseline does not say which line drove those. Peers' sharply below-consensus Q4 guides this month drew muted reactions (UAL -0.8% premarket, LUV +1% after hours).
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. JetBlue is down 45% in 20 sessions, Morgan Stanley and Goldman have cut estimates and targets for fuel, and UBS already uses $4.85. The unpriced part is the size of JetBlue's own Q4 margin, the size of its fuel recapture, and whether the 2026 guide is withdrawn. If fully priced, peers' muted reactions suggest the guide alone would not move JBLU much.
evidence.independence: Southwest Q4 at $4.55/gal (https://whtc.com/2026/10/21/southwest-airlines-cuts-2026-profit-forecast-as-fuel-costs-spike/); UBS $4.85 Q4 assumption (https://goldesel.de/aktien/news/jetblue-airways-aktie-ubs-stuft-auf-neutral-hoch-senkt-kursziel-auf-350-us-dollar).

evidence.text: The balance sheet is the line this print turns on, and the facts point both ways. (a) A senior creditor group holding the $2bn TrueBlue-backed 2031 notes and the ~$742m secured loan has hired PJT Partners and Akin Gump (WSJ/Bloomberg, 2026-10-24/25). The notes fell to 42 cents from ~80 earlier in October and the stock fell ~16% on 2026-10-26. (b) Against that, June 30 liquidity was $2.17bn of cash and investments plus an undrawn $600m revolver, against a $750m quarter-end minimum-liquidity covenant on the TrueBlue debt. UBS estimates ~$660m of H2 burn at $4.85 Q4 fuel and ~$1.6bn year-end liquidity, plus a possible $250m draw on a facility agreed in Q2. Scheduled debt repayments are only $236m for the rest of 2026 and $478m in 2027, and the company claims >$6bn of unencumbered assets. The 10:00 ET call is management's first chance to answer the creditor news. A Sept 30 liquidity figure well above the covenant reassures; an announced liability-management plan or adviser hire dilutes.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July 2026 the 2031 notes fell to 84 cents and JetBlue scheduled a fixed-income investor meeting on liquidity (Bloomberg, 2026-07-23). The Q2 print that followed reacted +10.5%. That is one precedent where a liquidity scare before the print was followed by relief.
evidence.why_not_priced: The creditor news is priced, with a 16% drop on 2026-10-26 and bonds at 42. What is not priced is the company's own Sept 30 liquidity number and its answer. Bonds at 42 imply a high restructuring probability inside about a year, while UBS's arithmetic puts year-end liquidity at about twice the covenant. If the market believed UBS, the notes would not trade at 42. Financing is a question here: no new company financing has been announced, so there is nothing yet to sign on use of proceeds. The sign stays near zero with a very wide band.
evidence.independence: The creditor hire is also reported at https://onemileatatime.com/news/jetblue-creditors-hire-advisers-stock-bonds-sink-bankruptcy-looms/ (2026-10-24) and https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/10/26/jetblue-airways-tumbles-16-as-creditors-hire-restructuring-advisers-united-airlines-rises-3-delta-edges-higher/ (2026-10-26). The liquidity and maturity schedule is at https://viewfromthewing.com/jetblue-stock-fell-below-3-how-close-is-bankruptcy-and-will-united-buy-it/ (2026-10-21) and the Q2 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001158463/000115846326000076/ex991-earningsreleaseq22026.htm). The UBS liquidity view is secondhand, via goldesel/FMP. One fact (the balance sheet) supports both readings, which is why they are filed as one finding.

The risk sits on the Q4 guide and on 2027 commentary. A small offset: TrendForce reports systems shifting from 96/128GB to 32/64GB RDIMMs from 3Q26, which means more modules, and so more RCDs, per bit.
